<details><summary><strong>ERM-P031 — User-journey and consumer-consequence service reliability</strong> — <code>SERVICE_RELIABILITY_PROPERTY</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P031

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
User-journey and consumer-consequence service reliability

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
High-availability service engineering, SRE SLIs/SLOs and end-to-end operational monitoring.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION`, `SOFTWARE_RELIABILITY_LINEAGE`, `CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION`, `RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE`, `CONVERGENT_PROPERTY`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Measure request success/latency and service uptime.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
Component or aggregate request metrics can remain green while critical multi-step journeys, user classes, freshness, durability or partial service fail.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
Named consumer journey achieves correct, timely, sufficiently fresh/durable outcome over the relevant window and dependencies.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Request-weighted average hides a small user cohort, tail latency, dependency path, stale data, partial outage or repeated short disruptions.

**MECHANISM**  
Define journey-level outcomes; stratify consumers and consequence; include tails/freshness/durability; measure dependency and degraded-state success.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
Externally consumed software/service whose important outcomes span components, dependencies or multiple steps.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
For simple single-step services, one end-to-end functional probe plus incident review may be sufficient.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Consumer definitions, telemetry across journey, privacy-preserving correlation, state correctness, dependency observability and denominator governance.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Aligns service reliability decisions with actual utility rather than local uptime.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
End users, mission/business owner, service owner and on-call operator.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Synthetic probe differs from real user; missing client-side failures; aggregation; bot/request volume dominates; rare critical journey underweighted.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
User happiness is multidimensional and difficult to reduce to a ratio; measurement itself can be incomplete or inequitable.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Machine/process uptime evolved toward request outcomes, tails, user journeys, cohorts, freshness and consequence.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
A small set of end-to-end, cohort-aware, consequence-linked measures with diagnostic drill-down and explicit blind spots.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
A dashboard or “golden signals” panel is not the property; current evidence that consumers receive required outcomes is.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
SERVICE_RELIABILITY_PROPERTY

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
Meta’s DNS servers were locally operational but users could not reach services; GitLab separated code-repository integrity from database data loss (SRC-059, SRC-060).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
No single user-journey metric covers all consequences; qualitative incident evidence and targeted tests remain necessary.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
How should reliability protect low-volume high-consequence consumers without allowing arbitrary metric proliferation?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

**EVIDENCE_STRENGTH**
- `HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE_TO_HIGH`
- `FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `HIGH`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`

**PRIMARY_SOURCES**  
[SRC-063](https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/), [SRC-064](https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/), [SRC-083](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

**CRITICAL_SOURCES**  
[SRC-058](https://aws.amazon.com/message/41926/), [SRC-059](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/10/05/networking-traffic/outage-details/), [SRC-060](https://about.gitlab.com/blog/postmortem-of-database-outage-of-january-31/), [SRC-066](https://www.usenix.org/publications/loginonline/what-sre-could-be), [SRC-067](https://www.usenix.org/conference/srecon23americas/presentation/goins)

**MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: User-journey and consumer-consequence service reliability
- `REQUIRED_FUNCTION`: Named consumer journey achieves correct, timely, sufficiently fresh/durable outcome over the relevant window and dependencies.
- `MISSION_OR_SERVICE`: Named consumer journey achieves correct, timely, sufficiently fresh/durable outcome over the relevant window and dependencies.
- `OPERATING_PROFILE`: Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.
- `ENVIRONMENT`: Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.
- `FAILURE_DEFINITION`: Request-weighted average hides a small user cohort, tail latency, dependency path, stale data, partial outage or repeated short disruptions.
- `DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE`: Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.
- `MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND`: Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.
- `CONSUMER`: End users, mission/business owner, service owner and on-call operator.
- `CHEAP_PATH`: For simple single-step services, one end-to-end functional probe plus incident review may be sufficient.
- `MATURE_FORM`: A small set of end-to-end, cohort-aware, consequence-linked measures with diagnostic drill-down and explicit blind spots.

**FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: User-journey and consumer-consequence service reliability
- `INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE`: Request-weighted average hides a small user cohort, tail latency, dependency path, stale data, partial outage or repeated short disruptions.
- `LOCAL_EFFECT`: Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.
- `NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT`: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
- `END_EFFECT`: Request-weighted average hides a small user cohort, tail latency, dependency path, stale data, partial outage or repeated short disruptions.
- `PROPAGATION_PATH`: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.
- `CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY`: A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.
- `DEPENDENCIES`: Consumer definitions, telemetry across journey, privacy-preserving correlation, state correctness, dependency observability and denominator governance.
- `COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING`: Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.
- `LATENT_CONDITION`: Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.
- `DETECTION`: Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.
- `CONTROL`: Define journey-level outcomes; stratify consumers and consequence; include tails/freshness/durability; measure dependency and degraded-state success.
- `RESIDUAL_RISK`: Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

**REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE**
- `APPLICABLE`: `false`
- `REASON`: The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: User-journey and consumer-consequence service reliability
- `TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES`: Request-weighted average hides a small user cohort, tail latency, dependency path, stale data, partial outage or repeated short disruptions.
- `OBSERVABLES`: Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.
- `DETECTION_COVERAGE`: Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.
- `FALSE_ALARM_COST`: Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.
- `MISSED_DETECTION_COST`: Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.
- `ISOLATION_RESOLUTION`: Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.
- `AMBIGUITY_GROUPS`: Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.
- `LATENCY`: Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.
- `CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION`: Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.
- `OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION`: Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.
- `RECOVERY_COVERAGE`: A detected fault counts only if the prescribed action restores or contains the target failure with known coverage.
- `MATURE_FORM`: A small set of end-to-end, cohort-aware, consequence-linked measures with diagnostic drill-down and explicit blind spots.

**RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE**
- `APPLICABLE`: `false`
- `REASON`: No distinct recovery claim is made by this candidate.

**RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: User-journey and consumer-consequence service reliability
- `CLAIM`: A small set of end-to-end, cohort-aware, consequence-linked measures with diagnostic drill-down and explicit blind spots.
- `POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR`: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
- `CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY`: Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.
- `OPERATIONAL_PROFILE`: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
- `TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN`: Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.
- `MODEL`: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
- `ASSUMPTIONS`: Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.
- `CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY`: Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.
- `CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS`: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
- `COVERAGE`: Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.
- `DECISION_OR_CONSUMER`: End users, mission/business owner, service owner and on-call operator.
- `CHEAP_PATH`: For simple single-step services, one end-to-end functional probe plus incident review may be sufficient.
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE`: No single user-journey metric covers all consequences; qualitative incident evidence and targeted tests remain necessary.
- `EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS`: Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.
- `MATURE_FORM`: A small set of end-to-end, cohort-aware, consequence-linked measures with diagnostic drill-down and explicit blind spots.

</details>
<details><summary><strong>ERM-P032 — SLI/SLO and error-budget governance as a scoped decision aid</strong> — <code>USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_GAMED</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P032

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
SLI/SLO and error-budget governance as a scoped decision aid

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
Google SRE practice and subsequent industrial adoption/critique.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION`, `DOMAIN_SPECIFIC`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION`, `DOMAIN_TRANSLATION`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Set an SLO below 100%, measure bad events, and spend the error budget to balance reliability and change velocity.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
Teams need an operational threshold linking observed service outcomes to release, stabilisation and alert decisions.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
A user/mission-relevant outcome remains within an agreed loss budget over a declared denominator/window, with action when exhausted.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Easy metric chosen; time/event denominator mismatch; cohort/tail hidden; maintenance excluded; budget treated as permission; chronic exhaustion creates nonsense.

**MECHANISM**  
Select user-relevant SLI; document denominator/window/exclusions; use burn-rate/tail/cohort views; preagree actions; review validity and gaming.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
Repeatable online service with measurable consumer outcomes and cross-functional authority to act on budget state.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
Use direct incident/change judgement for small or low-volume services where a stable ratio is misleading.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Reliable telemetry, user-journey mapping, stakeholder agreement, release authority, dependency awareness and review cadence.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Creates a common, current decision signal and makes reliability/change trade-offs explicit.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
Service owner, product/change authority, on-call and users represented by the SLI.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Nine-count branding; denominator manipulation; omitted cohorts; short/long outage equivalence; chronic debt; threshold chosen backwards from current performance.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
Boolean ratios fit request/response better than many other services; correct error-budget response and alert thresholds remain contested.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Uptime targets evolved toward user-focused SLIs, multiwindow burn rates, policy actions and explicit critique of denominator/threshold assumptions.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
A revisable, consumer-grounded governance instrument used alongside incident, dependency and tail evidence—not a universal reliability score.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
The SLO dashboard and error-budget ritual are optional; the property is a valid current decision boundary and agreed response.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_GAMED

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
SRE practice supplies detailed operational mechanisms, while practitioner critiques identify denominator, threshold and chronic-budget failure modes (SRC-063–SRC-067).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
No robust multi-organisation evidence establishes one SLO formula or error-budget policy as universally optimal.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
What empirical decision rules best respond to budget exhaustion across different service archetypes and consequence distributions?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

**EVIDENCE_STRENGTH**
- `HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_TO_MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `CONTEXT_DEPENDENT`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`

**PRIMARY_SOURCES**  
[SRC-063](https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/), [SRC-065](https://sre.google/workbook/error-budget-policy/), [SRC-083](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

**CRITICAL_SOURCES**  
[SRC-066](https://www.usenix.org/publications/loginonline/what-sre-could-be), [SRC-067](https://www.usenix.org/conference/srecon23americas/presentation/goins), [SRC-058](https://aws.amazon.com/message/41926/), [SRC-059](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/10/05/networking-traffic/outage-details/)

<details><summary><strong>ERM-P033 — End-to-end health checks and symptom-versus-cause separation</strong> — <code>DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROPERTY</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P033

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
End-to-end health checks and symptom-versus-cause separation

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
Built-in test/liveness checks, model-based diagnosis and SRE symptom-oriented monitoring.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`DIAGNOSTICS_AND_PHM_LINEAGE`, `SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION`, `HYBRID`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE`, `SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION`, `HYBRID_RESOLUTION`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Poll component liveness and page on unhealthy status.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
A component heartbeat can be green while the actual path is unusable; conversely a symptom can identify impact without establishing cause.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
Detect end-to-end functional loss quickly while preserving a separate evidence path for causal diagnosis.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Shallow probe; cached/static response; monitor bypasses dependency/state/authentication; probe shares failure; symptom automatically labelled root cause.

**MECHANISM**  
Use layered probes: end-to-end outcome for impact, component/dependency signals for diagnosis; test probe coverage/failure; validate after recovery.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
Remote automated service, failover, load balancer health, readiness/liveness, synthetic transactions or auto-remediation.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
A direct user-visible transaction is often cheaper and stronger than many internal health bits.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Representative journey, safe test account/data, independent monitoring path, timing and known blind spots.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Reduces false-green availability and shortens diagnosis without confusing symptom with mechanism.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
On-call operator, automated traffic manager, incident commander and users.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Probe not representative; synthetic succeeds while cohort fails; health endpoint isolated from data plane; monitor unavailable; causal overreach.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
Deep probes can be costly, create load or mutate state; they cannot cover all semantic outcomes.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Single component heartbeat evolved toward layered end-to-end functional monitoring, cohort telemetry and dependency diagnosis.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
A documented coverage stack: user/mission outcome detection, diagnostic signals, independent probe health and post-recovery validation.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
A green checkmark is not the property; observed required function plus understood coverage is.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROPERTY

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
Meta’s DNS servers were operational but unreachable, a direct example of a locally green component and failed service path (SRC-059).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
No finite set of health checks proves absence of latent or unknown semantic failure.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
How can probe representativeness be continuously estimated as user journeys and dependencies change?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

**EVIDENCE_STRENGTH**
- `HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_TO_MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `HIGH`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`

**PRIMARY_SOURCES**  
[SRC-024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.arcontrol.2004.12.002), [SRC-026](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6391061/), [SRC-064](https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/)

**CRITICAL_SOURCES**

<details><summary><strong>ERM-P034 — Explicit dependency, correlation and hidden single-point mapping</strong> — <code>REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROPERTY</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P034

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
Explicit dependency, correlation and hidden single-point mapping

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
RBD/FTA serial structures, supply/logistics analysis and modern cloud/service dependency mapping.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE`, `SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION`, `CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE`, `SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION`, `SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY`, `CONVERGENT_PROPERTY`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Represent series/parallel component dependencies in an RBD.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
Architecture diagrams omit shared DNS, identity, control planes, libraries, regions, suppliers, spares, people or change channels that dominate failure.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
Every dependency necessary for the critical function or its recovery is identified with consequence, alternatives and correlation.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Unknown transitive dependency; fallback uses same provider/control; SLA substitutes for observed performance; human/on-call or logistics bottleneck omitted.

**MECHANISM**  
Discover runtime and organisational dependencies; classify criticality/failure domains; test fallback; record correlated change/maintenance; monitor supplier performance.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
End-to-end service, outsourced/supplier component, multi-region design, recovery plan, shared platform or long logistics chain.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
For simple systems, trace one critical user/mission path and its recovery path rather than build a universal service map.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Telemetry/tracing, contracts plus observed data, architecture and support knowledge, ownership and change notifications.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Exposes serial reliability and common-cause risks that component metrics and nominal redundancy hide.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
Architect, service/fleet owner, supplier manager, operator, continuity planner and mission owner.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Dynamic discovery gaps; shadow dependency; circular fallback; shared credentials; control-plane dependence; concentrated maintainer/supplier.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
Maps go stale quickly and can become inventory ceremony; causal dependence is richer than static edges.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Static blocks evolved toward dynamic, transitive, control/state/human/supply dependency and correlated-change models.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
A decision-focused dependency model refreshed by telemetry and incidents, including recovery dependencies and credible fallback evidence.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
A service map is not the property; knowing which shared dependency can defeat required function and what is done about it is.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROPERTY

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
AWS, Meta and CrowdStrike incidents demonstrate storage, backbone/DNS and shared supplier/update dependencies with broad correlated impact (SRC-058, SRC-059, SRC-061, SRC-062).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
Dependency elimination is impossible; some shared platforms improve reliability through expertise and scale, so the property is visibility and evidence, not universal decentralisation.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
How can hidden control-plane and organisational dependencies be discovered before a failure removes the discovery tools?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

- `FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_TO_MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`

[SRC-005](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/staff/sr0492/), [SRC-023](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19720006837/downloads/19720006837.pdf), [SRC-052](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/contract/cr6268/), [SRC-063](https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/)

**MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: Explicit dependency, correlation and hidden single-point mapping
- `REQUIRED_FUNCTION`: Every dependency necessary for the critical function or its recovery is identified with consequence, alternatives and correlation.
- `MISSION_OR_SERVICE`: Every dependency necessary for the critical function or its recovery is identified with consequence, alternatives and correlation.
- `OPERATING_PROFILE`: Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.
- `ENVIRONMENT`: Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.
- `FAILURE_DEFINITION`: Unknown transitive dependency; fallback uses same provider/control; SLA substitutes for observed performance; human/on-call or logistics bottleneck omitted.
- `DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE`: Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.
- `MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND`: Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.
- `CONSUMER`: Architect, service/fleet owner, supplier manager, operator, continuity planner and mission owner.
- `CHEAP_PATH`: For simple systems, trace one critical user/mission path and its recovery path rather than build a universal service map.
- `MATURE_FORM`: A decision-focused dependency model refreshed by telemetry and incidents, including recovery dependencies and credible fallback evidence.

**FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: Explicit dependency, correlation and hidden single-point mapping
- `INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE`: Unknown transitive dependency; fallback uses same provider/control; SLA substitutes for observed performance; human/on-call or logistics bottleneck omitted.
- `LOCAL_EFFECT`: Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.
- `NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT`: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
- `END_EFFECT`: Unknown transitive dependency; fallback uses same provider/control; SLA substitutes for observed performance; human/on-call or logistics bottleneck omitted.
- `PROPAGATION_PATH`: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.
- `CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY`: A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.
- `DEPENDENCIES`: Telemetry/tracing, contracts plus observed data, architecture and support knowledge, ownership and change notifications.
- `COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING`: Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.
- `LATENT_CONDITION`: Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.
- `DETECTION`: Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.
- `CONTROL`: Discover runtime and organisational dependencies; classify criticality/failure domains; test fallback; record correlated change/maintenance; monitor supplier performance.
- `RESIDUAL_RISK`: Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

**REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: Explicit dependency, correlation and hidden single-point mapping
- `REDUNDANCY_FORM`: Active, standby, voting, diverse, replicated or alternate-path redundancy as explicitly declared.
- `CLAIMED_TOLERANCE`: The specified number/class of faults tolerated while meeting required function or an accepted degraded state.
- `FAILURE_DOMAINS`: Physical, power, network, control-plane, state, software, supplier, operator and maintenance domains.
- `INDEPENDENCE_EVIDENCE`: Evidence must address shared causes rather than infer independence from copy count or labels.
- `COMMON_CAUSE_COUPLINGS`: Specification, design, implementation, environment, supplier, maintenance, configuration and operational coupling.
- `STANDBY_LATENCY_OR_DORMANCY`: Dormant faults, activation delay and cold/warm/hot readiness are measured when applicable.
- `SWITCHOVER_COVERAGE`: Detection, decision, transfer, state synchronisation and post-transfer functional success.
- `STATE_CONSISTENCY`: The takeover state and authority must be current, complete and semantically valid.
- `DEGRADED_MODE`: Declared reduced capability and exit conditions.
- `TEST_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE`: Representative failover/failure tests plus field or incident evidence where available.
- `MATURE_FORM`: A decision-focused dependency model refreshed by telemetry and incidents, including recovery dependencies and credible fallback evidence.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE**
- `APPLICABLE`: `false`
- `REASON`: The candidate is not a diagnostic claim; outcome observation may still be required by its evidence profile.

**RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE**
- `APPLICABLE`: `false`
- `REASON`: No distinct recovery claim is made by this candidate.

**RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE**
- `APPLICABLE`: `false`
- `REASON`: The property is primarily a design/operation mechanism; its validation still follows ERM-P026–P029.

<details><summary><strong>ERM-P035 — Hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation</strong> — <code>CONTEXT_DEPENDENT</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P035

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
Hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
Hardware/software fault injection, dependability validation and 2010s chaos engineering.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`FAULT_INJECTION_OR_CHAOS_TRANSLATION`, `FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPUTING_LINEAGE`, `DOMAIN_SPECIFIC`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY`, `DOMAIN_TRANSLATION`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Inject component or service failures to see whether redundancy/recovery works.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
Analytical claims about detection, containment, degradation and recovery can remain untested in the integrated current system.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
Discriminate a live reliability uncertainty for a specified fault, profile, boundary and decision without causing disproportionate harm.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Random breakage; nonrepresentative fault; weak oracle; no decision consumer; production risk exceeds value; repeated ritual after claim already established.

**MECHANISM**  
State hypothesis/steady-state metric; choose representative fault and blast radius; predefine abort; observe full recovery/postconditions; record decision/update.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
Material integrated uncertainty not cheaply resolved by static analysis, simulation, staging or direct functional test.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
Use unit/integration test, simulation, replay or nonproduction exercise when it resolves the same uncertainty more safely/cheaply.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Containment, observability, recovery readiness, representative load/state, authorisation, abort/fallback and post-experiment analysis.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Finds integration/coverage gaps and supplies current empirical evidence for specific resilience claims.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
Service/mission owner, operator, reliability engineer and change authority.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Toy fault; survivorship; experiment itself causes outage; only steady-state metric checked; no state validation; outcomes not acted upon.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
Industrial evidence is advocacy-heavy; systematic review still finds evaluation and adoption gaps; production experimentation creates ethical/operational risk.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Fault injection evolved from component coverage testing toward hypothesis-driven system experiments with blast-radius and decision controls.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
A sparse portfolio of claim-bound experiments chosen by expected information value and closed through recovery validation and engineering action.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
“Chaos day,” monkey tooling or periodic failure ritual is not the property; decision-relevant falsification is.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
Meta’s long-running storm drills aided staged restoration but had never simulated global-backbone loss, illustrating both value and coverage limits (SRC-059).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
A successful experiment proves only the tested conditions; it never establishes general resilience.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
What empirical designs best estimate transfer from controlled experiments to rare correlated production failures?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `HIGH_FOR_TESTED_CLAIM`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE_TO_HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_TO_MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_WITHOUT_MATCH`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`

**RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: Hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation
- `CLAIM`: A sparse portfolio of claim-bound experiments chosen by expected information value and closed through recovery validation and engineering action.
- `POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR`: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
- `CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY`: Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.
- `OPERATIONAL_PROFILE`: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
- `TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN`: Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.
- `MODEL`: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
- `ASSUMPTIONS`: Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.
- `CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY`: Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.
- `CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS`: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
- `COVERAGE`: Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.
- `DECISION_OR_CONSUMER`: Service/mission owner, operator, reliability engineer and change authority.
- `CHEAP_PATH`: Use unit/integration test, simulation, replay or nonproduction exercise when it resolves the same uncertainty more safely/cheaply.
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE`: A successful experiment proves only the tested conditions; it never establishes general resilience.
- `EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS`: Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.
- `MATURE_FORM`: A sparse portfolio of claim-bound experiments chosen by expected information value and closed through recovery validation and engineering action.

<details><summary><strong>ERM-P036 — Overload-aware recovery: capacity margin, load shedding and bounded retries</strong> — <code>CONTEXT_DEPENDENT</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P036

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
Overload-aware recovery: capacity margin, load shedding and bounded retries

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
Queueing/capacity practice, high-availability service recovery and overload-control patterns.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION`, `AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE`, `HYBRID`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION`, `RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE`, `HYBRID_RESOLUTION`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Keep spare capacity, shed low-priority load and retry failed requests.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
Failure removes capacity while backlog/retries increase demand, so failover/restart can trigger a second collapse.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
Protect priority function and recover without unstable positive feedback or exhaustion of the remaining fault-tolerant capacity.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Retry storm; thundering herd; failover target underprovisioned; cache cold start; load shedding removes critical work; no admission control.

**MECHANISM**  
Reserve margin; classify load; cap/constrain retries; exponential backoff/jitter; circuit break; shed by priority; ramp recovery; test cold/failed capacity.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
Elastic/queued services, failover, regional loss, dependency slowdown, mass restart or bursty demand.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
Reject clearly and early rather than queue/retry when capacity is exhausted and work is safely repeatable later.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Demand/capacity observability, priority semantics, idempotency, queue limits, fallback and consumer communication.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Prevents recovery mechanisms from amplifying the initiating fault and preserves critical service.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
Operator, service owner, priority users and incident commander.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Incorrect priorities; hidden downstream bottleneck; stale capacity estimate; retries across many clients synchronise; shed work not recoverable.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
Spare capacity costs money/energy; load shedding can externalise harm and obscure underinvestment.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Static N+1 margin evolved toward dynamic admission, priority shedding, retry budgets and staged reconstitution.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
A measured stability envelope and failure-mode-specific overload policy, including consumer consequences and recovery postconditions.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
A circuit-breaker library or autoscaler is not the property; stable protected operation under the target loss is.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
AWS reported backlogs after S3 recovery; Meta explicitly avoided turning all services on at once because caches, power and systems could crash (SRC-058, SRC-059).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
For non-queued fixed-demand systems this property may not trigger; extra mechanisms can add complexity.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
How should retry/load-shed policies coordinate across independently owned clients and dependencies?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

- `FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`

- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_TO_MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `CONTEXT_DEPENDENT`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `HIGH`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`

**CRITICAL_SOURCES**

- `PROPERTY`: Overload-aware recovery: capacity margin, load shedding and bounded retries
- `INITIATING_FAILURE`: Retry storm; thundering herd; failover target underprovisioned; cache cold start; load shedding removes critical work; no admission control.
- `RECOVERY_ACTION`: Reserve margin; classify load; cap/constrain retries; exponential backoff/jitter; circuit break; shed by priority; ramp recovery; test cold/failed capacity.
- `AUTHORITY_SOURCE`: The designated current configuration/state authority and authorised operator or controller.
- `CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE`: Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.
- `RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND`: Explicit allowed state/data loss or “none” for state-continuous functions.
- `RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND`: Explicit time-to-restoration bound including diagnosis, logistics, repair and validation.
- `STATE_RECONCILIATION`: Resolve divergent, stale, partial or replayed state before authoritative service resumes.
- `FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS`: Protect priority function and recover without unstable positive feedback or exhaustion of the remaining fault-tolerant capacity.
- `DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS`: Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.
- `DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS`: Critical dependencies and capacity are verified rather than assumed from local restart.
- `VALIDATION`: Independent end-to-end functional and state checks under representative demand.
- `RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY`: Named human or automated authority with explicit acceptance criteria.
- `ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK`: A bounded fallback when restoration validation fails or the original cause persists.
- `MATURE_FORM`: A measured stability envelope and failure-mode-specific overload policy, including consumer consequences and recovery postconditions.

**RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE**
- `APPLICABLE`: `false`
- `REASON`: The property is primarily a design/operation mechanism; its validation still follows ERM-P026–P029.

</details>
<details><summary><strong>ERM-P037 — Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery</strong> — <code>RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P037

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
Built-in test/maintenance records, incident logging, flight/industrial recorders and service observability.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`DIAGNOSTICS_AND_PHM_LINEAGE`, `SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION`, `MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE`, `HYBRID`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE`, `SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION`, `CONVERGENT_PROPERTY`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Log faults and maintenance actions for troubleshooting and FRACAS.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
The initiating failure or automatic remediation destroys/overwrites telemetry, tools, clocks or state needed to diagnose, validate recovery and prevent recurrence.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
Retain sufficient trustworthy evidence to determine impact, state, likely causes, actions and post-recovery correctness within time/privacy constraints.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts.

**MECHANISM**  
Independent/remote telemetry paths; durable event/action records; time/identity correlation; bounded snapshots; evidence-preserving recovery mode; privacy/access governance.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
Complex automated systems, correlated outages, remote repair, stateful recovery or rare high-consequence events.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
For simple deterministic faults, record the minimal causal/action evidence rather than instrument everything.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Independent power/network/storage where warranted, data quality, clocks, access, retention, privacy and incident procedures.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Shortens diagnosis, supports state reconciliation and allows corrective-action effectiveness to be tested.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
Operator, maintainer, incident investigator, design owner and return-to-service authority.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Telemetry blind spot; observer overload; misleading stale metrics; data loss; sensitive evidence withheld; logs treated as ground truth.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
Observability can be costly, intrusive and security/privacy-sensitive; more data does not guarantee diagnosis.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Fault codes evolved toward distributed traces, event/state provenance, recovery journals and independent evidence channels.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
A logging stack is not the property; reliable evidence for live decisions and recurrence learning is.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
Meta lost normal and out-of-band access and many internal tools during the outage, directly showing diagnostic dependencies can fail with the system (SRC-059).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
In some failures independent physical inspection or direct test is more informative than extensive telemetry.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
How can evidence integrity and privacy be preserved when autonomous recovery acts faster than human review?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

**EVIDENCE_STRENGTH**
- `HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `VERY_HIGH`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_TO_MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `HIGH`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`

**PRIMARY_SOURCES**  
[SRC-010](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsSearch.aspx?q=MIL-HDBK-2155), [SRC-024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.arcontrol.2004.12.002), [SRC-056](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-184), [SRC-064](https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/)

**CRITICAL_SOURCES**  
[SRC-058](https://aws.amazon.com/message/41926/), [SRC-059](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/10/05/networking-traffic/outage-details/), [SRC-060](https://about.gitlab.com/blog/postmortem-of-database-outage-of-january-31/), [SRC-074](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.800-4)

- `PROPERTY`: Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery
- `INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE`: Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts.
- `LOCAL_EFFECT`: Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.
- `NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT`: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
- `END_EFFECT`: Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts.
- `PROPAGATION_PATH`: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.
- `CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY`: A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.
- `DEPENDENCIES`: Independent power/network/storage where warranted, data quality, clocks, access, retention, privacy and incident procedures.
- `COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING`: Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.
- `LATENT_CONDITION`: Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.
- `DETECTION`: Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.
- `CONTROL`: Independent/remote telemetry paths; durable event/action records; time/identity correlation; bounded snapshots; evidence-preserving recovery mode; privacy/access governance.
- `RESIDUAL_RISK`: Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

**REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE**
- `APPLICABLE`: `false`
- `REASON`: The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery
- `TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES`: Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts.
- `OBSERVABLES`: Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.
- `DETECTION_COVERAGE`: Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.
- `FALSE_ALARM_COST`: Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.
- `MISSED_DETECTION_COST`: Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.
- `ISOLATION_RESOLUTION`: Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.
- `AMBIGUITY_GROUPS`: Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.
- `LATENCY`: Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.
- `CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION`: Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.
- `OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION`: Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.
- `RECOVERY_COVERAGE`: A detected fault counts only if the prescribed action restores or contains the target failure with known coverage.
- `MATURE_FORM`: Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.

**RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE**

- `INITIATING_FAILURE`: Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts.
- `RECOVERY_ACTION`: Independent/remote telemetry paths; durable event/action records; time/identity correlation; bounded snapshots; evidence-preserving recovery mode; privacy/access governance.
- `AUTHORITY_SOURCE`: The designated current configuration/state authority and authorised operator or controller.

- `RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND`: Explicit time-to-restoration bound including diagnosis, logistics, repair and validation.
- `STATE_RECONCILIATION`: Resolve divergent, stale, partial or replayed state before authoritative service resumes.
- `FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS`: Retain sufficient trustworthy evidence to determine impact, state, likely causes, actions and post-recovery correctness within time/privacy constraints.
- `DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS`: Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.
- `DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS`: Critical dependencies and capacity are verified rather than assumed from local restart.
- `VALIDATION`: Independent end-to-end functional and state checks under representative demand.
- `RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY`: Named human or automated authority with explicit acceptance criteria.
- `ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK`: A bounded fallback when restoration validation fails or the original cause persists.
- `MATURE_FORM`: Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.

**RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery
- `CLAIM`: Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.
- `POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR`: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
- `CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY`: Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.
- `OPERATIONAL_PROFILE`: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
- `TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN`: Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.
- `MODEL`: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
- `ASSUMPTIONS`: Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.
- `CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY`: Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.
- `CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS`: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
- `COVERAGE`: Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.
- `DECISION_OR_CONSUMER`: Operator, maintainer, incident investigator, design owner and return-to-service authority.
- `CHEAP_PATH`: For simple deterministic faults, record the minimal causal/action evidence rather than instrument everything.
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE`: In some failures independent physical inspection or direct test is more informative than extensive telemetry.
- `EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS`: Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.
- `MATURE_FORM`: Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.

<details><summary><strong>ERM-P038 — Proportional cheap path and deterministic functional check</strong> — <code>STRONGLY_RETAINED</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P038

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
Proportional cheap path and deterministic functional check

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
Tailoring in military/NASA R&M, objectives-based dependability management and decision-focused testing.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE`, `CONVERGENT_PROPERTY`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Tailor the reliability programme to mission class and risk.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
Full FMEA, probabilistic model, demonstration, SLO or chaos programme can cost more than the uncertainty it resolves and become ceremony.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
Obtain enough trustworthy evidence for the actual decision at proportionate cost and risk.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Mandatory artefact regardless of consequence; model precision without decision sensitivity; repeated test after result cannot change action; analysis delays simple fix.

**MECHANISM**  
State decision/uncertainty/consequence; ask whether a direct functional check, conservative bound, simple design change or acceptance is sufficient; escalate only when needed.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
Every proposed reliability activity; especially low-consequence, reversible, small-scope or already-observable work.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
This property is the cheap path: simplest evidence/mechanism that resolves the live decision while preserving critical assumptions.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Clear decision consumer, consequence, reversibility, uncertainty and authority to tailor.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Preserves engineering attention for material failure risks and resists reliability bureaucracy.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
Decision owner, mission/service owner and engineering team.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Under-analysis disguised as agility; consequence underestimated; direct check misses latent/tail risk; tailoring used to avoid inconvenient evidence.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
Proportionality is judgement-sensitive and can rationalise weak assurance; explicit rationale and triggers for escalation are needed.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Prescriptive activity lists increasingly coexist with objectives-based, tailored, decision-relevant R&M practice.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
A documented minimum-sufficient path with escalation criteria, not a blanket waiver or blanket process.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
No named artefact is privileged; only the evidence/mechanism needed for the decision survives.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
STRONGLY_RETAINED

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
Incident reports support targeted safeguards and tests tied to actual mechanisms rather than indiscriminate activity expansion (SRC-058–SRC-061).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
High-consequence irreversible missions often justify expensive evidence even when probability is low.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
Can value-of-information thresholds be operationalised without turning proportionality itself into a new ceremony?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

- `LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_TO_MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `MODERATE`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`

<details><summary><strong>ERM-P039 — Retirement of stale controls, metrics, support and reliability claims</strong> — <code>RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM</code></summary>

**PROPERTY_ID**  
ERM-P039

**PROPERTY_NAME**  
Retirement of stale controls, metrics, support and reliability claims

**HISTORICAL_ORIGIN**  
Configuration/obsolescence management, field-data refresh and metric-governance practice.

**LINEAGE_CLASS**  
`MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE`, `SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION`, `CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING`

**RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS**  
`MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE`, `SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION`, `CONVERGENT_PROPERTY`

**ORIGINAL_FORM**  
Review reliability predictions, maintenance plans and support resources periodically.

**PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED**  
Controls, thresholds, spares, procedures, models and dashboards persist after configuration/profile/consumer change and create false assurance or burden.

**REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION**  
Only current, decision-relevant reliability controls and support capabilities govern the current system.

**FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT**  
Obsolete spare/tool; unsupported dependency; stale profile; dead alert; inherited “nine”; old backup format; handbook rate for changed technology.

**MECHANISM**  
Attach owner, scope, evidence, configuration, review/expiry and retirement trigger; monitor obsolescence; remove or replace controls that no longer discriminate risk.

**TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT**  
Technology/configuration/profile/consumer change, repeated false alarms, unused metric, support deprecation or expired evidence.

**NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH**  
Delete a stale metric/control when no consumer or decision can be named; retain a simple direct check if still useful.

**DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS**  
Inventory and ownership, configuration/dependency change signals, evidence lineage and authority to retire contractual/process residue.

**OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS**  
A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

**FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS**  
A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

**REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS**  
No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS**  
Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

**RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS**  
No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

**MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS**  
Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

**EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF**  
Reduces false confidence, alert/maintenance burden and unsupported recovery dependence.

**DECISION_OR_CONSUMER**  
System/service owner, maintainer, operator, procurement and assurance authority.

**KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES**  
Zombie dashboard; contract inertia; metric tied to bonus; unsupported library/part; retirement removes latent protection; no replacement evidence.

**IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS**  
Frequent change can erode comparability and institutional memory; retirement needs archival trace and consequence check.

**HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED**  
Periodic document review broadened to live evidence freshness, control efficacy, dependency support and obsolescence risk.

**MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM**  
Every material reliability control has a current consumer, evidence basis, configuration scope, expiry and safe retirement/replacement path.

**CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY**  
Keeping a metric because it exists is ceremony; deliberate retention or retirement is the property.

**CURRENT_STATUS**  
RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE**  
The MIL-HDBK-217 critique shows how outdated data/models can persist institutionally after technology changes (SRC-047).

**CONTRARY_EVIDENCE**  
Long-lived controls may encode rare lessons; deletion without historical analysis can reintroduce old failure modes.

**OPEN_QUESTIONS**  
What evidence should trigger retirement when the protected failure is rare and absence may reflect the control’s success?

**DISPOSITION_RATIONALE**  
Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

**EVIDENCE_STRENGTH**
- `HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`
- `INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE_TO_HIGH`
- `OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH`: `LOW_TO_MODERATE`
- `TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH`: `HIGH`
- `ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY`: `HIGH`
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH`: `MODERATE`

**MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: Retirement of stale controls, metrics, support and reliability claims
- `REQUIRED_FUNCTION`: Only current, decision-relevant reliability controls and support capabilities govern the current system.
- `MISSION_OR_SERVICE`: Only current, decision-relevant reliability controls and support capabilities govern the current system.
- `OPERATING_PROFILE`: Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.
- `ENVIRONMENT`: Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.
- `FAILURE_DEFINITION`: Obsolete spare/tool; unsupported dependency; stale profile; dead alert; inherited “nine”; old backup format; handbook rate for changed technology.
- `DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE`: Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.
- `MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND`: Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.
- `CONSUMER`: System/service owner, maintainer, operator, procurement and assurance authority.
- `CHEAP_PATH`: Delete a stale metric/control when no consumer or decision can be named; retain a simple direct check if still useful.
- `MATURE_FORM`: Every material reliability control has a current consumer, evidence basis, configuration scope, expiry and safe retirement/replacement path.

- `REASON`: No distinct propagation claim is made by this candidate.

**DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE**
- `APPLICABLE`: `false`
- `REASON`: The candidate is not a diagnostic claim; outcome observation may still be required by its evidence profile.

**RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE**

**RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE**
- `PROPERTY`: Retirement of stale controls, metrics, support and reliability claims
- `CLAIM`: Every material reliability control has a current consumer, evidence basis, configuration scope, expiry and safe retirement/replacement path.
- `POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR`: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
- `CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY`: Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.
- `OPERATIONAL_PROFILE`: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
- `TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN`: Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.
- `MODEL`: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
- `ASSUMPTIONS`: Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.
- `CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY`: Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.
- `CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS`: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
- `COVERAGE`: Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.
- `DECISION_OR_CONSUMER`: System/service owner, maintainer, operator, procurement and assurance authority.
- `CHEAP_PATH`: Delete a stale metric/control when no consumer or decision can be named; retain a simple direct check if still useful.
- `CONTRARY_EVIDENCE`: Long-lived controls may encode rare lessons; deletion without historical analysis can reintroduce old failure modes.
- `EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS`: Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.
- `MATURE_FORM`: Every material reliability control has a current consumer, evidence basis, configuration scope, expiry and safe retirement/replacement path.
