## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_MISSION_FAILURE_MODEL

The primitive object is not a component failure rate; it is a **mission contract**:

\[
\mathcal{M}=\langle I,F,C,O,E,D,G,T,K,B\rangle
\]

where `I` is the item/system boundary, `F` the required function, `C` the consumer, `O` the operating profile and modes, `E` the environment, `D` the demand/duty cycle, `G` the success/failure/degradation scoring rule, `T` the mission interval or demand count, `K` the configuration identity and `B` the consequence/decision boundary. A defensible mission reliability statement is therefore of the form:

\[
R_{\mathcal{M}}=P(\text{no defined functional failure during }T\mid I,F,C,O,E,D,G,K,B).
\]

This expression is deliberately conditional. It does not say that probability is always the cheapest evidence. A deterministic end-to-end functional check may dominate for low-consequence, reversible work. Nor does it collapse availability or restoration into reliability.

### Required state semantics

At minimum distinguish: `NOMINAL`; `ACCEPTABLE_DEGRADED`; `FAILED_UNDETECTED`; `DETECTED_NOT_ISOLATED`; `DIAGNOSED_OR_CONTAINED`; `UNDER_MAINTENANCE_OR_REPAIR`; `RESTORED_PENDING_VALIDATION`; and `RETURNED_TO_SERVICE`. Intermittent, partial, latent and false-indication states require explicit scoring. A component may be alive while the required system function is failed; a service may respond while its result is stale, semantically wrong or unusable; a closed ticket may leave the recurrence mechanism intact.

### Failure attribution and denominator

The consequence claim uses the end-to-end boundary; causal correction may use nested component/dependency boundaries. Responsibility, contract scope and physical causation are not interchangeable. Planned windows, third-party failures, maintenance states, retries and degraded cohorts cannot be silently removed from a denominator merely because they complicate a metric.

### Mission-reliability profile admission test

1. Name the function and consumer.
2. State profile, environment, mission phase, interval/demands and configuration.
3. Define complete, partial, intermittent, latent and acceptable degraded outcomes.
4. State who scores ambiguous cases and how missing observations are treated.
5. Identify the cheapest evidence that would change the decision.
6. Expire the claim when any material condition changes.

Sources: [SRC-020](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2004.2), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-030](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-038](https://www.cto.mil/sea/rm/), [SRC-063](https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_RELIABILITY_AVAILABILITY_MAINTAINABILITY_MODEL

Reliability, availability and maintainability answer different conditional questions.

| Attribute | Defensible question | Typical mathematical object | What it does **not** establish |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reliability | Will the defined function avoid defined failure through the mission/demands? | Survival/no-failure probability or demand success | Fast repair, current availability, useful degraded service |
| Point availability | Is the defined function capable at time `t`? | State probability `P(X(t) ∈ acceptable states)` | Few failures, acceptable tails or correct state |
| Interval/operational availability | What share/probability of an interval is the function capable under actual support? | Up time divided by total calendar/exposure time, with declared exclusions | Equal consequence for all minutes/users; independence |
| Maintainability | Given a repairable failure and support conditions, how quickly/probably can restoration be completed? | `M(t)=P(T_restore ≤ t | failure, support)` | That the item rarely fails or that the support organisation is ready |
| Supportability | Are spares, tools, data, facilities, skills and logistics available when needed? | Delay distributions, fill rates and resource-state models | Maintainable physical design by itself |
| Durability/life | How does irreversible degradation/wear limit useful life? | Lifetime/degradation distribution | Availability during life or service restoration |

For a repairable system, total downtime is not just hands-on repair:

\[
T_D=T_{detect}+T_{diagnose}+T_{authorise/access}+T_{logistics}+T_{active\ repair}+T_{state\ reconcile}+T_{validate}.
\]

A simple steady-state expression such as `A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR)` is valid only for a narrow alternating-process model and a consistent definition of means. It omits administrative/logistics delay, multiple states, imperfect repair, dependence, planned work and consequence weighting. `Inherent availability`, `achieved availability` and `operational availability` therefore cannot be substituted without their support and maintenance boundaries.

The mature form is a small decision-fit state model, not a maximally populated RAM dashboard. Sources: [SRC-009](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=54046), [SRC-030](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-031](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-032](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-036](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-051](https://doi.org/10.1214/088342306000000448).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_FAILURE_PROPAGATION_MODEL

A fault is a hypothesised or observed cause/condition; an error is an incorrect internal state; a failure is externally relevant deviation from required function. The chain may be immediate, latent, intermittent, masked, cascading or activated only by a later demand. This taxonomy is useful only when tied to a declared boundary and consumer.

### Complementary analyses

- **FMEA/FMECA** is generally bottom-up: function/item → mode → local effect → next-level effect → end effect → detection/control/criticality.
- **FTA** is generally top-down: top event → combinations/causes → cut sets → qualitative or conditional quantitative reasoning.
- **Event/dynamic/state analysis** becomes necessary when order, repair, standby activation, timing, software state or operator action changes outcomes.
- **Field/incident analysis** challenges omissions and dependence that static models did not represent.

The mature failure-propagation record names: initiating fault/failure; local, enclosing and mission effects; propagation mechanism; containment region; latent conditions; shared dependencies; detection and control; residual risk; configuration; and evidence that the control works. A row labelled “mitigated” without implemented and verified prevention, detection, containment, recovery or acceptance is open.

Systematic analysis survives; the universal worksheet does not. Focused interface and failure-path challenge is the cheap path when a full model would not change a decision. Sources: [SRC-004](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=37027), [SRC-005](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/staff/sr0492/), [SRC-020](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2004.2), [SRC-035](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-052](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/contract/cr6268/), [SRC-079](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cosrev.2015.03.001).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_LIFE_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEM_MODEL

### Non-repairable lifetime

For lifetime `T`, survival is `R(t)=P(T>t)`, distribution `F(t)=1-R(t)`, density `f(t)` where it exists, and hazard `h(t)=f(t)/R(t)`. Exponential life imposes constant hazard. Weibull, lognormal, gamma, competing-risk and mixture models answer different descriptive or mechanistic questions. A good fit does not identify the mechanism; censoring, selection, field returns, environment and use covariates can dominate.

The “bathtub curve” is not a law. Infant mortality, approximately constant hazard and wear-out can arise in some populations, but mixtures, maintenance, screening, changing use and competing mechanisms can produce different or apparent shapes. Age-based replacement pays only where conditional failure risk changes with age in a way that action can improve at acceptable consequence and intervention risk.

### Repairable recurrent events

Repairable-system data are event histories, not independent component lifetimes. Choose the process according to repair semantics:

- a renewal process assumes the post-repair item is effectively as-good-as-new for the modelled mechanism;
- a homogeneous Poisson process/exponential model assumes constant event intensity and independent increments;
- an NHPP permits time-varying cumulative intensity, including power-law/Crow forms;
- imperfect/minimal-repair or generalised renewal models are needed when repair changes “virtual age” only partially;
- multi-state and Markov/semi-Markov models may be needed for degradation, standby, logistics and repair phases.

Pool neither unit-hours nor repeated demands as independent without evidence. Report event definition, exposure clock, repair action, recurrent-event identity, truncation/censoring, configuration and profile. Model selection should be driven by the estimand and decision, not the prettiest fit.

Sources: [SRC-001](https://doi.org/10.1115/1.4010337), [SRC-007](https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/citations/AD0789105), [SRC-008](https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA066579.pdf), [SRC-021](https://books.google.com/books?id=0VxRAAAAMAAJ), [SRC-022](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/book/10.1137/1.9781611971194), [SRC-040](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/apr.htm), [SRC-043](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/section3/apr311.htm), [SRC-046](https://doi.org/10.1109/TR.2002.804492), [SRC-051](https://doi.org/10.1214/088342306000000448).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_MODEL

For independent, perfectly covered parallel elements with component reliabilities `R_i`, the familiar success probability is:

\[
R_{parallel}=1-\prod_i(1-R_i).
\]

This is not a generic redundancy dividend. It assumes the system succeeds when any qualifying path succeeds; component events have the required independence; detection, switching and adjudication work; state and capacity are adequate; and no shared dependency defeats all paths. Real claims therefore require a dynamic profile:

1. required function and tolerated fault class;
2. active/standby/voting/diverse architecture and degraded capacity;
3. physical, power, network, control-plane, state, software, supplier, operator and maintenance failure domains;
4. beta-factor/explicit common-cause or other dependence evidence where quantification is used;
5. dormant standby condition and activation latency;
6. detection/decision/transfer coverage;
7. fencing, authority and state reconciliation;
8. post-switchover functional validation and return path;
9. representative field/fault-injection evidence and configuration expiry.

`Two copies` is not `two failure domains`; a backup is not an available standby; different code is not independent specification or model assumptions; automated failover is not correct failover. Diversity may reduce selected common modes but can increase interface, adjudicator, testing and maintenance complexity. A simpler robust component plus tested restoration may dominate when consequence and repair time permit.

Sources: [SRC-011](https://www.rand.org/pubs/papers/P817.html), [SRC-013](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1985.231893), [SRC-014](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1986.6312924), [SRC-015](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1985.231895), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-052](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/contract/cr6268/), [SRC-054](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20240013667), [SRC-055](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ress.2006.09.004).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_MODEL

Detection, isolation and recovery coverage are separate conditional claims.

- `Detection coverage(m, o, e, Δt)` is the probability or demonstrated fraction that mode/failure `m` is recognised in operating state `o`, environment `e`, within latency `Δt`.
- `Isolation coverage` adds resolution: which replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group is established strongly enough to act?
- `Recovery coverage` asks whether the selected action actually contains/restores the required function.

A diagnostic profile must declare target fault population, observables, thresholds, latency, ambiguity groups, confidence/calibration, false-positive cost, false-negative cost, action authority and drift/freshness. Overall accuracy can be meaningless when rare high-consequence failures or class imbalance matter. A root-cause label is a hypothesis until discriminated from correlated symptoms and shared dependencies.

One health bit is defensible only when it directly tests the required function, including state, freshness, dependencies and capacity. Otherwise use layered outcome checks, residuals and dependency signals. Automation must abstain/escalate when confidence or operating-profile support is insufficient.

Sources: [SRC-024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.arcontrol.2004.12.002), [SRC-025](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymssp.2005.09.012), [SRC-026](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6391061/), [SRC-027](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1856/5844/), [SRC-064](https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/), [SRC-072](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ress.2025.112110).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_GRACEFUL_DEGRADATION_MODEL

Graceful degradation is not “keep anything running.” It is a controlled transition into a predeclared acceptable state:

\[
x \in A_{degraded}(consumer, mission\ phase, duration, consequence).
\]

The record must identify protected and sacrificed functions, minimum capacity/quality/freshness, prioritised consumers, observability, allowed duration, entry/exit criteria, operator/user communication, and recovery path. Degradation that is invisible, unbounded or unable to preserve state correctness is failure, not grace.

`Fail-safe`, `fail-stop` and `fail-operational` are contextual objectives. Continue when the residual function and state remain demonstrably acceptable and stopping imposes greater consequence. Contain/stop when authority, correctness, propagation or consequence cannot be bounded. Safety and security are recorded only as source-established constraints on the reliability objective, not imported as substitute analyses.

Load shedding, feature disablement, reduced precision, read-only mode, manual fallback and priority service are mature only when mission semantics make the trade explicit. Sources: [SRC-020](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2004.2), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-058](https://aws.amazon.com/message/41926/), [SRC-063](https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/), [SRC-081](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenix-03/analysis-causes-and-costs-failures-internet-services).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_RECOVERY_RESTORATION_MODEL

Recovery is an end-to-end state transition, not a verb such as restart, retry or failover. A mature path is:

`detect → contain → diagnose/authorise → select trusted recovery source → restore/rebuild/reconfigure → reconcile authoritative state → verify dependencies/capacity → verify required function → return to service → monitor recurrence`.

### Required bounds and postconditions

- `RPO/state-loss bound`: allowed loss, staleness, duplicate/replay or divergence.
- `RTO/restoration bound`: includes detection, diagnosis, access/authorisation, logistics, active repair/rebuild, state reconciliation and validation.
- source postcondition: backup/checkpoint/replica/spare is integral, accessible, compatible and not subject to the same failure;
- state postcondition: authority, completeness, freshness, ordering and consistency meet mission criteria;
- dependency postcondition: upstream/downstream services, identity, DNS/control planes, network, storage and capacity are ready;
- functional postcondition: representative end-to-end outcomes meet required thresholds;
- return-to-service authority and fallback are explicit.

Retries require transient classification, bounded budgets, backoff/jitter and idempotency/deduplication where effects can repeat. Checkpoint/restart requires valid checkpoint state and rollback semantics. Failover requires fencing and takeover capacity. Rollback requires a compatible prior configuration and state transition. Rebuild requires trusted specifications, dependencies and data. None is universal.

Restoration exercises must be realistic enough to challenge people, tooling, permissions, timing, dependencies and state—not only the happy script. Evidence expires with material configuration or organisational change. Sources: [SRC-012](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1975.6312842), [SRC-016](https://www.hpl.hp.com/techreports/tandem/TR-85.7.pdf), [SRC-056](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-184), [SRC-057](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.1339), [SRC-060](https://about.gitlab.com/blog/postmortem-of-database-outage-of-january-31/), [SRC-078](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11227-013-0884-0), [SRC-082](https://doi.org/10.1145/844128.844132).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_MAINTAINABILITY_REPAIRABILITY_MODEL

Maintainability is engineered jointly in the item and its support system. Design mechanisms include modularity, accessibility, safe isolation, replaceability, test points, built-in test, standard interfaces, configuration/state transfer, remote operability and post-repair verification. Operational mechanisms include procedures, current documentation, tools, test equipment, spares, facilities, skills, permissions, logistics, maintenance windows and escalation.

A maintainability demonstration must use actual or representative field conditions, not only a bench task. Report the restoration-time distribution and its components, not only mean active repair time. Tail delay, ambiguity, rare spares, travel, approvals and data/state reconciliation often dominate. Modularity is beneficial only when replacement preserves configuration, calibration, authority and interface compatibility.

Maintenance-induced failure is a system mechanism: opening, handling, misassembly, contamination, wrong part/software/configuration, incomplete test, documentation ambiguity, workload and organisational pressure. Human factors therefore change design, tooling and procedure requirements rather than assigning blame.

Obsolescence and unsupported dependencies can invalidate maintainability even when the original design was repairable. The mature property includes a retirement/substitution plan for stale tools, parts, knowledge and support claims. Sources: [SRC-009](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=54046), [SRC-020](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2004.2), [SRC-031](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-032](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-060](https://about.gitlab.com/blog/postmortem-of-database-outage-of-january-31/), [SRC-076](https://www.faa.gov/about/initiatives/maintenance_hf), [SRC-077](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/document-library/general-publications/european-plan-aviation-safety-epas-2025).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_MAINTENANCE_POLICY_MODEL

Maintenance policy is a decision under failure mechanism, consequence, observability, intervention risk and support cost—not a maturity ladder in which “predictive” always wins.

| Policy | Trigger conditions | Principal evidence burden | Typical failure of the policy | Cheap alternative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Run to failure | Failure consequence and restoration time are acceptable; no useful precursor/age relation | Consequence, spares and restoration evidence | Hidden secondary damage or support delay | Simple spare/procedure check |
| Age-based replacement/rework | Conditional failure risk rises materially with age and intervention reduces it | Age–risk relation, replacement effectiveness, induced-failure cost | Universal calendar replacement; bathtub assumption | Inspection or run-to-failure |
| Condition-based/on-condition | A detectable potential-failure condition exists with a usable P–F interval | Coverage, latency, threshold, false alarms and action lead time | Sensor/threshold misses; action too late | Periodic functional inspection |
| Predictive/RUL | Forecast uncertainty changes a real maintenance decision | Calibration, drift, transfer, cost-sensitive decision evaluation | Precise-looking but non-actionable RUL; false maintenance | Condition threshold or schedule |
| Opportunistic/grouped | Shared downtime/access makes joint work efficient | Dependency and induced-work analysis | Scope growth and correlated maintenance fault | Minimal necessary task |
| Risk-based/RCM | Functions, failure modes and consequences differ materially | Functional failure, consequence and policy-effect evidence | Worksheet ritual or subjective criticality | Focused high-consequence review |
| Redesign/remove task | Failure/maintenance mechanism dominates lifecycle burden | Corrective-action effectiveness and configuration evidence | Workaround institutionalised without cause removal | Targeted design fix |

Predictive maintenance earns retention only where the observation precedes functional failure with enough lead time, uncertainty is calibrated, the intervention changes outcome, and net consequence beats simpler policies. Sources: [SRC-008](https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA066579.pdf), [SRC-025](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymssp.2005.09.012), [SRC-034](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-071](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.1943), [SRC-072](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ress.2025.112110), [SRC-073](https://doi.org/10.1177/16878132261438568).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_RELIABILITY_GROWTH_FRACAS_MODEL

Duane and Crow/AMSAA-style models describe cumulative failure intensity trends under specific recurrent-event assumptions. They are useful for planning and monitoring but do not identify why reliability changed. A decreasing estimated intensity can arise from effective fixes, learning, selected scoring, maturity of the test population, censored modes, profile drift, removed hard cases or simple randomness.

A mature test–analyse–fix/FRACAS loop is:

1. bind failure report to configuration, profile, environment and exposure;
2. preserve symptom, state and evidence;
3. classify failure family and recurrence relationship;
4. distinguish proximate trigger, enabling conditions and causal mechanism;
5. choose correction, containment or accepted residual risk;
6. implement under change/configuration control;
7. verify the changed mechanism and regress affected functions;
8. observe comparable exposure and recurrence;
9. update the model/claim and retire stale controls.

The causal unit is the intervention and its verified effect, not the closed ticket or improving line. Delayed fixes, imperfect repair, multiple configurations and targeted versus representative test exposure must be visible. When samples are small, a transparent failure-family/fix/regression ledger is a better cheap path than a fitted growth curve.

Sources: [SRC-006](https://doi.org/10.1109/TA.1964.4319640), [SRC-007](https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/citations/AD0789105), [SRC-010](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsSearch.aspx?q=MIL-HDBK-2155), [SRC-048](https://doi.org/10.17226/18987), [SRC-084](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsSearch.aspx?q=MIL-HDBK-189C).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_MODEL

A reliability-evidence packet must identify:

`claim; required function; estimand; population/denominator; configuration; profile/environment; failure oracle; sampling/exposure; model; assumptions; censoring/missingness; uncertainty/confidence; failure-mode and path coverage; contrary evidence; consumer/decision; and expiry`.

### Demonstration

A pass is not a reliability level unless sample size/exposure, failure criterion, independence/dependence, confidence and stopping rule support that inference. For `n` independent Bernoulli demands with zero failures, a one-sided lower confidence bound is conditional on that model (for significance `α`, `R_L=α^(1/n)`). It is not zero risk, does not identify the lifetime distribution and does not cover unrepresented demand classes or common-cause dependence. Recurrent unit-hours require the appropriate event-process model.

### Accelerated evidence

Acceleration is credible only when the stress–life relation and failure mechanism transfer to use conditions. Competing mechanisms, threshold effects, multiple stresses, changing material/software behaviour and extrapolation dominate uncertainty. “Highly accelerated” methods may expose weaknesses but are not automatically quantitative field-life demonstrations.

### Field evidence and calibration

Field data are closer to actual use but suffer missing events, censoring, changing configurations, unknown denominators, reporting/repair selection and heterogeneous environments. Prediction, qualification, fault injection and field experience should triangulate; none automatically dominates every question. Intervals and contrary cases are retained. Evidence expires after material configuration, profile, environment, supplier, model, support or dependency change.

Evidence strength is partitioned into historical provenance, formal/probabilistic validity, life/field strength, demonstration strength, incident support, operational practice, replication, transferability, assumption sensitivity and contrary evidence. A strong model with weak transfer is labelled as such.

Sources: [SRC-033](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-037](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-040](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/apr.htm), [SRC-042](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/section1/apr16.htm), [SRC-045](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/section3/apr31a.htm), [SRC-047](https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/18987/chapter/17), [SRC-049](https://www.iapsam.org/PSAM16/papers/DA21-PSAM16.pdf), [SRC-050](https://doi.org/10.1080/08982112.2014.964413).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_SOFTWARE_SERVICE_RELIABILITY_MODEL

Software faults do not generally wear out like physical parts; they are activated by inputs, state, timing, dependencies and configuration. Reliability testing therefore needs an operational profile and explicit failure oracle. Continuous change makes evidence freshness central.

For services, an SLI is an observed indicator, an SLO is a scoped target, and an error budget is a governance mechanism for action. They are useful only when the indicator represents an important consumer outcome and the policy actually constrains decisions. Request-weighted success can hide complete failure for a small cohort, a critical transaction, freshness/durability loss, tail latency or correlated regional outage. Important user journeys, cohort/tenant/region views and multi-window burn rates are stronger forms.

Incident response, on-call, observability, canaries, rollback and toil reduction contribute reliability mechanisms, but SRE is a **service translation**, not the universal endpoint. “Blameless” learning can fail when it becomes a ritual that avoids accountable system change; blame can also suppress evidence. Closure is implemented correction plus recurrence monitoring.

A service returned by a load balancer can still be semantically unavailable; a remaining error budget does not automatically justify any risky change; lower incident count does not establish lower failure risk. Sources: [SRC-019](https://doi.org/10.1109/52.199724), [SRC-063](https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/), [SRC-064](https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/), [SRC-065](https://sre.google/workbook/error-budget-policy/), [SRC-066](https://www.usenix.org/publications/loginonline/what-sre-could-be), [SRC-067](https://www.usenix.org/conference/srecon23americas/presentation/goins), [SRC-081](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenix-03/analysis-causes-and-costs-failures-internet-services), [SRC-083](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_DEPENDENCY_CORRELATION_MODEL

A reliability block diagram or service map is an abstraction of a success path, not the system itself. Mature dependency analysis includes:

- serial/parallel functional dependencies and capacity thresholds;
- power, cooling, network, DNS, identity, storage and control planes;
- shared regions/providers, third-party services and suppliers;
- common libraries, build/release tooling, configuration and data/model pipelines;
- authoritative state, clocks, queues and retry feedback;
- operators, on-call, permissions, procedures and communication channels;
- spares, facilities, test equipment and logistics;
- correlated maintenance/change and recovery dependencies.

Edges need type and correlation, not merely adjacency. A dependency can be latent until failover/recovery. Contract/SLA language is not observed reliability and external ownership is not independence. Maps should be refreshed from telemetry, change records, fault tests and incidents; otherwise they become stale ceremony.

Field cases are decisive negative evidence: AWS S3’s control operation removed excessive capacity and impaired dependent services; Meta’s backbone change disconnected data centres and DNS reachability; GitLab discovered unusable/incomplete recovery paths; the CrowdStrike update propagated through a shared software/change channel at global scale. These cases do not prove universal rates, but they establish mechanisms that any credible dependency model must be able to represent. Sources: [SRC-023](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19720006837/downloads/19720006837.pdf), [SRC-052](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/contract/cr6268/), [SRC-058](https://aws.amazon.com/message/41926/), [SRC-059](https://engineering.fb.com/2021/10/05/networking-traffic/outage-details/), [SRC-060](https://about.gitlab.com/blog/postmortem-of-database-outage-of-january-31/), [SRC-061](https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/falcon-content-update-preliminary-post-incident-report/), [SRC-062](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2024/07/20/helping-our-customers-through-the-crowdstrike-outage/).

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_METRIC_PROXY_MODEL

A reliability metric may govern a decision only after its numerator/denominator, clock, boundary, profile, consequence, missingness, confidence and manipulation path are explicit. Means are not automatically wrong; they are incomplete when tails, mixtures, cohorts or correlated events drive consequence.

| Metric/proxy | Legitimate use | Hidden assumption | Gaming/misuse path | Mature replacement/supplement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MTBF | Summarise mean inter-failure time or reciprocal constant intensity for a defined repairable process. | Stable process/event definition; often HPP when used as `1/λ`. | Pool unlike units/time; hide hazard/trend/tails; call it mission reliability. | Mission reliability plus recurrent-event trend/tail and downtime burden. |
| MTTF/mean life | Compare a non-repairable lifetime distribution/population. | Population/profile and finite meaningful mean. | Hide early/tail failures and mechanism; mix censored returns. | Survival quantiles/hazard with intervals and mechanism covariates. |
| MTTR | Summarise a defined restoration-time component. | Consistent start/stop and support boundary. | Start after diagnosis; exclude logistics/validation; close on restart. | Restoration-time distribution and total downtime decomposition. |
| MDT/downtime | Measure time function is unavailable. | State/failure scoring and complete clocks. | Exclude planned windows, partial users or degraded states. | Consumer-weighted state occupancy and tail restoration. |
| Availability/uptime | Summarise capability over time for a defined function. | Correct state oracle, denominator and consequence weighting. | Five-nines branding; average away cohorts/correlations. | Journey/cohort availability, outage-event/tail profile and state validity. |
| Incident count/severity count | Track reported operational events/families. | Stable detection/reporting/severity/exposure. | Suppress/reclassify/split/merge events; ignore latent risk. | Exposure- and consequence-normalised recurrence families. |
| SLO attainment/error budget | Govern service action against a scoped consumer indicator. | Indicator validity and an enforceable decision policy. | Change denominator/window; exclude cohorts; spend budget automatically. | Journey-specific objectives, burn, exception audit and outcome checks. |
| Failure rate | Estimate event intensity for a stated process/time basis. | Model/process and exposure clock. | Assume stationarity; average trends/mixtures; ignore dependence. | Time/covariate-dependent recurrent-event model and uncertainty. |
| Defect density | Track known defect counts per size/release. | Stable detection and size/complexity measure. | Optimise classification/size; treat faults as failures. | Operational failure outcomes and risk-weighted defect families. |
| Test hours/demands | Report exposure accumulated under a test design. | Representative profile and independent/dependent trial semantics. | Count idle/easy hours; omit rare critical cases; no confidence. | Stratified exposure/coverage plus bounded demonstration inference. |
| Reliability score/composite | Communicate a multidimensional summary. | Transparent weights, monotonicity and decision validation. | Compensate catastrophic weakness with unrelated strong metrics. | Small vector of non-substitutable mission, recovery and support bounds. |
| Health-check pass rate | Monitor a specific observable/path. | End-to-end validity and known diagnostic coverage. | Check local liveness only; ignore stale/corrupt/dependent service. | Functional journey checks plus calibrated diagnostic signals. |

### Decision-admission rule

Before a metric governs design, release, maintenance or acceptance, require: named decision/consumer; required function; numerator and denominator; clock and exclusions; operational profile; failure/restoration oracle; uncertainty; tail/cohort/correlation treatment; configuration identity; manipulation test; and evidence expiry. When that burden exceeds the value of the decision, use the cheap direct functional check and make no broader reliability claim.

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_CEREMONY_STRIPPING_LEDGER

| Named artefact/ritual | Underlying property | Artefact required? | Capture/failure path | Frozen IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FMEA worksheet | Systematically challenge plausible modes, effects, propagation and controls. | No. A focused functional/interface analysis may be cheaper and better. | Rows copied, ranks manipulated, controls unverified. | ERM-P006, P045 |
| MTBF target | Bound mission failure frequency/burden for a defined process and profile. | No. Reliability over mission/demand or recurrent-event intensity may be the right estimand. | Constant hazard, tail and dependence hidden. | ERM-P001, P005, P026, P041 |
| Redundancy diagram | Make failure domains, success logic, capacity, state and switchover assumptions explicit. | No. Any inspectable architecture/evidence form suffices. | Copy count treated as independence; standby and control plane omitted. | ERM-P008, P009, P051 |
| SLO dashboard | Expose current consumer-relevant service state to a decision process. | No. A small direct journey check can be better for simple systems. | Denominator/cohort gaming; indicator not mission. | ERM-P031, P032, P042 |
| Chaos day/game day | Empirically discriminate a live fault-tolerance or recovery uncertainty. | Only when the experiment can change a decision and risk is bounded. | Random spectacle, safe toy faults, no closure. | ERM-P035, P050 |
| Backup-success indicator | Establish that recoverable authoritative state exists and remains usable. | No. Restore/reconstitution evidence is required, not only copy completion. | Unreadable, stale, incomplete, incompatible or dependent backup. | ERM-P017, P046 |
| Disaster-recovery exercise | Challenge a declared recovery path under realistic conditions. | Only when scope, configuration and expiry are explicit; one exercise is not universal proof. | Script rehearsed while dependencies/capacity/state are omitted. | ERM-P016–P018, P047 |
| Postmortem/FRACAS closure | Convert failure evidence into causal correction and recurrence control. | No named template is required; causal closure is. | Ticket closed, action generic, fix unverified. | ERM-P024, P025, P048 |
| Green health bit | Detect a failure relevant to the required function early enough to act. | No. End-to-end checks or multi-signal diagnosis may be necessary. | Liveness proxies mask semantic/state/dependency failure. | ERM-P011–P013, P033, P049 |
| Reliability-growth curve | Estimate/monitor recurrent failure trend under a declared model. | No. Failure families and verified fixes can be more decision-relevant. | Post-hoc model and causal overclaim. | ERM-P024, P025, P053 |
| Predictive-maintenance/AI badge | Provide actionable lead time or bounded automated diagnosis/remediation with net value. | Only where mechanism, calibration, drift, authority and verification are established. | False maintenance, opaque confidence, action cascade, transfer failure. | ERM-P023, P052, P055 |
| “Five nines” certificate | Summarise scoped availability evidence for a named consumer/path/window. | No universal scalar. | Excluded windows, request weighting and correlated tails hidden. | ERM-P031, P032, P042 |

The frozen rule is: retain the mechanism that changes a decision or failure path; remove the named artefact when it adds no evidence. Periodicity is justified by evidence freshness and expected decision value, not by ritual cadence.

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_CRITICISM_LEDGER

| ID | Criticism target | Criticism | Evolution disposition | Mature response | Sources | Properties |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CR-01 | METRIC_OR_PROXY | MTBF used without a defined mission/process or with an untested constant-hazard assumption. | REFINED | Retain means only as one statistic; require failure process, interval/demand and tails. | SRC-040, SRC-043, SRC-046 | ERM-P005, P026, P041 |
| CR-02 | LIFE_OR_FAILURE_MODEL | The bathtub curve is overgeneralised from selected populations and mechanisms. | NARROWED | Use mechanism- and population-specific hazard evidence; mixtures and maintenance are explicit. | SRC-008, SRC-041, SRC-046 | ERM-P022, P028, P043 |
| CR-03 | PREDICTION_MODEL | Handbook part-count/stress prediction is treated as field truth despite input/model uncertainty. | REPLACED | Use as conditional comparative input at most; calibrate with test and field evidence. | SRC-039, SRC-047, SRC-048 | ERM-P027–P029, P044 |
| CR-04 | FAILURE_ANALYSIS_METHOD | FMEA becomes a worksheet/checklist with subjective ranks and no verified control closure. | REFINED | Retain systematic failure challenge; strip the mandatory form and link modes to evidence. | SRC-004, SRC-035, SRC-079 | ERM-P006, P025, P045 |
| CR-05 | FAILURE_ANALYSIS_METHOD | FTA completeness and quantification inherit top-event, boundary and independence omissions. | REFINED | Use explicit ground rules, common-cause events, dynamic analysis and empirical challenge. | SRC-005, SRC-052, SRC-053, SRC-079 | ERM-P004, P006, P008 |
| CR-06 | REDUNDANCY_OR_FAULT_TOLERANCE | Common-cause failures defeat nominally redundant channels. | GENERALIZED | Count failure domains and shared causes; qualify redundancy benefit conditionally. | SRC-052, SRC-054, SRC-055 | ERM-P008, P009, P034, P051 |
| CR-07 | REDUNDANCY_OR_FAULT_TOLERANCE | Standby/switchover is latent-bad, too slow, capacity-deficient or state-incompatible. | REFINED | Treat takeover as a complete diagnostic/state/capacity recovery path. | SRC-028, SRC-056, SRC-058–SRC-060 | ERM-P009, P016–P018 |
| CR-08 | REDUNDANCY_OR_FAULT_TOLERANCE | N-version software failures are correlated despite independent teams. | NARROWED | Diversity is only conditional common-mode mitigation with empirical independence evidence. | SRC-013–SRC-015 | ERM-P040 |
| CR-09 | DIAGNOSTICS | Alarm/health status is substituted for fault isolation or end-function truth. | GENERALIZED | Separate detection, diagnosis, recovery coverage and independent functional checks. | SRC-024–SRC-027, SRC-064 | ERM-P011–P013, P033, P049 |
| CR-10 | MAINTENANCE_POLICY | Scheduled preventive maintenance is applied without age relation and can induce failure. | NARROWED | Use age-based work only with a valid age mechanism and net consequence benefit. | SRC-008, SRC-076, SRC-077 | ERM-P021, P022 |
| CR-11 | MAINTENANCE_POLICY | Predictive maintenance overclaims transfer, RUL precision and universal superiority. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | Require observable precursor, calibrated uncertainty, actionable lead time and comparison with simpler policies. | SRC-025, SRC-026, SRC-071, SRC-072 | ERM-P023, P052 |
| CR-12 | RELIABILITY_GROWTH | Growth curves are fitted after selected fixes and interpreted causally. | REFINED | Retain trend models but require prospective fixes, stable exposure and recurrence evidence. | SRC-006, SRC-007, SRC-048, SRC-084 | ERM-P024, P025, P053 |
| CR-13 | DEMONSTRATION_OR_TEST | Zero failures is read as zero risk or as identifying the lifetime distribution. | REJECTED | Only bounded inference at stated confidence under sampling/dependence assumptions survives. | SRC-049, SRC-050 | ERM-P026, P054 |
| CR-14 | DEMONSTRATION_OR_TEST | Accelerated stress activates a different mechanism from field use. | NARROWED | Require physical/statistical acceleration-model validation and competing-risk checks. | SRC-037, SRC-045 | ERM-P027 |
| CR-15 | DEMONSTRATION_OR_TEST | Long tests use an unrepresentative operational profile and miss rare critical inputs. | REFINED | Bind evidence to explicit profile, environment and consequence-important cases. | SRC-019, SRC-080 | ERM-P002, P026, P030 |
| CR-16 | SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION | Uptime and request averages hide partial, stale, tail and cohort-specific failures. | GENERALIZED | Measure important journeys, cohorts and consequences; retain scoped SLOs as aids. | SRC-063, SRC-066, SRC-067 | ERM-P031, P032, P042 |
| CR-17 | METRIC_OR_PROXY | Incident counts are gamed by detection/reporting/severity/denominator changes. | REFINED | Use recurrence families, exposure and consequence evidence, not count alone. | SRC-033, SRC-048, SRC-061 | ERM-P025, P028, P048 |
| CR-18 | CEREMONIAL_RELIABILITY_PROGRAMME | Postmortems/FRACAS close without design change or effectiveness verification. | REFINED | Close only on implemented, configuration-bound action and recurrence monitoring. | SRC-010, SRC-048, SRC-066 | ERM-P024, P025 |
| CR-19 | RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR | Backups exist but cannot restore, or restoration returns inconsistent/incorrect state. | GENERALIZED | Recovery evidence includes source integrity, reconciliation, functional/state/dependency postconditions. | SRC-056, SRC-057, SRC-060 | ERM-P016, P017, P046 |
| CR-20 | RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR | Plans are unexercised or one scripted failover is overgeneralised. | REFINED | Exercise representative failure/reconstitution families; bind scope and expiry. | SRC-056, SRC-057 | ERM-P017, P047 |
| CR-21 | SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION | Chaos engineering becomes unrepresentative fault injection without a decision consumer. | NARROWED | Only hypothesis-, claim- and decision-bound experiments survive. | SRC-068–SRC-070 | ERM-P035, P050 |
| CR-22 | REDUNDANCY_OR_FAULT_TOLERANCE | Auto-remediation/retries amplify overload, duplicate effects or recurring corruption. | GENERALIZED | Bound retries, shed load, isolate state and verify postconditions; stop loops. | SRC-058, SRC-059, SRC-081, SRC-082 | ERM-P018, P036, P055 |
| CR-23 | MAINTAINABILITY | Low active repair time ignores diagnosis, access, logistics, validation and support delays. | GENERALIZED | Use total-downtime decomposition and actual field capability. | SRC-009, SRC-031, SRC-032, SRC-060 | ERM-P019, P020 |
| CR-24 | CEREMONIAL_RELIABILITY_PROGRAMME | Qualification evidence is carried across configuration, environment, supplier or support changes. | REJECTED | Evidence is versioned and expires under material change. | SRC-028, SRC-033, SRC-061, SRC-062 | ERM-P029, P039 |
| CR-25 | METRIC_OR_PROXY | “Five nines” omits denominator, exclusions and correlated outage consequence. | REJECTED | Retain only scoped, consumer-relevant availability evidence. | SRC-063, SRC-066, SRC-067 | ERM-P031, P032, P042 |
| CR-26 | DIAGNOSTICS | AI/ML diagnostic confidence, drift and automated authority are unbounded. | STILL_CONTESTED | Admit only narrow use cases with calibration, monitoring, abstention, reversible action and independent verification. | SRC-071, SRC-072, SRC-074, SRC-075 | ERM-P055 |

Criticism is aimed at five distinct objects: the underlying property, its model assumptions, its implementation, its metric/proxy and its ceremonial programme. Most underlying properties were preserved or generalised; universalised models and proxy substitutions were narrowed or rejected.

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_EVOLUTION_UNDER_CRITICISM

| Earlier form | Evolved form | Disposition | What changed | Properties | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Component MTBF | Mission/user-journey reliability | GENERALIZED | Function, profile, failure state and consumer become prior to the scalar. | ERM-P001–P005 | SRC-028, SRC-030, SRC-063 |
| Independent parallel blocks | Failure-domain/common-cause-aware redundancy | REFINED | Independence, coverage, standby, state and capacity are evidenced rather than assumed. | ERM-P008, P009, P034, P040 | SRC-052, SRC-054, SRC-055 |
| Failure prevention only | Detection, containment, degradation, recovery and repair | GENERALIZED | Reliable service can include bounded degradation and validated restoration. | ERM-P010–P018 | SRC-020, SRC-028, SRC-056 |
| Corrective repair after design | Diagnosability and maintainability-by-design | REFINED | Access, isolation, replaceability, testability and support are architecture properties. | ERM-P019–P021 | SRC-009, SRC-031, SRC-032 |
| Universal scheduled maintenance | Mechanism/consequence-based maintenance policy | NARROWED | Age-based, condition-based and run-to-failure policies are selected by failure behaviour and decision value. | ERM-P021–P023 | SRC-008, SRC-071, SRC-072 |
| Prediction handbook output | Calibrated multi-source evidence | REPLACED | Prediction is one conditional input alongside demonstration and current field data. | ERM-P026–P029 | SRC-033, SRC-047, SRC-048 |
| One health bit | Mode-indexed detection and end-to-end functional diagnosis | GENERALIZED | Coverage, ambiguity, latency, false alarms and recovery action are explicit. | ERM-P011–P013, P033 | SRC-024–SRC-027, SRC-064 |
| Backup existence | Tested restoration and reconstitution | GENERALIZED | Integrity, accessibility, authority, reconciliation and functional validation define closure. | ERM-P016, P017 | SRC-056, SRC-057, SRC-060 |
| Uptime percentage | Consumer consequence and SLO/user-journey measures | GENERALIZED | Scoped SLOs govern action but do not become universal truth. | ERM-P031, P032 | SRC-063, SRC-066, SRC-067 |
| Incident response | Closed-loop corrective design and recurrence control | REFINED | Learning closes only when causes/conditions are changed and effectiveness observed. | ERM-P024, P025 | SRC-010, SRC-048, SRC-066 |
| Random fault injection | Hypothesis- and decision-bound reliability experiment | NARROWED | Experiment value is discriminating a live uncertainty under safe controls. | ERM-P035 | SRC-068–SRC-070 |
| Average failure rate | Tail, recurrent, correlated and common-mode exposure | GENERALIZED | Process shape, recurrence, mixture populations and dependence are modelled explicitly. | ERM-P008, P026–P028, P034 | SRC-046, SRC-051, SRC-052 |
| Software fault count | Operational-profile failure behaviour | REFINED | Failure activation depends on inputs, state, change and environment rather than wear-out. | ERM-P030 | SRC-017–SRC-019, SRC-080 |
| Failover completion | Mission/state/dependency postconditions | GENERALIZED | Restoration is an observed end state, not a control-plane event. | ERM-P016–P018 | SRC-056, SRC-058–SRC-060 |
| Static dependency diagram | Configuration- and incident-refreshed correlation map | REFINED | Control planes, suppliers, people and logistics are included as failure dependencies. | ERM-P004, P034, P039 | SRC-058, SRC-059, SRC-061 |
| Maintenance task time | Total operational downtime and support capability | GENERALIZED | Diagnosis, access, logistics, state repair and validation join active repair. | ERM-P019, P020 | SRC-009, SRC-031, SRC-032 |
| Automated diagnosis/remediation | Authority-bounded, independently verified automation | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | No general payoff is admitted; calibration, drift and action safety remain live burdens. | ERM-P055 | SRC-074, SRC-075 |

Not every evolution solved the originating problem. Current SLO practice can still be gamed; common-cause probabilities remain sparse; predictive-maintenance transfer remains weak; chaos experiments can remain unrepresentative; and rapidly changing software/model configurations can invalidate evidence faster than conventional qualification cycles.

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_INTERNAL_TENSIONS

<details><summary><strong>T-01 — Redundancy versus Complexity/common cause</strong> — <code>PERSISTENT</code></summary>

**TENSION_ID**  
T-01

**POLE_A**  
Redundancy

**POLE_B**  
Complexity/common cause

**WHY_GENUINE**  
Extra channels can tolerate independent faults but add shared control, state, maintenance and operating paths.

**TRIGGER**  
A single failure is intolerable and credible domain separation exists.

**FAILURE_IF_A_DOMINATES**  
Cost/coordination and correlated faults dominate.

**FAILURE_IF_B_DOMINATES**  
Single points remain unmitigated.

**MATURE_RESOLUTION**  
Model failure domains, coverage, state and capacity; compare simpler robustness/recovery.

**CHEAP_PATH**  
For low consequence, use one robust implementation plus direct restore evidence.

**EVIDENCE**  
SRC-052, SRC-054, SRC-055

**STATUS**  
PERSISTENT

</details>

<details><summary><strong>T-02 — Preventive maintenance versus Maintenance-induced failure</strong> — <code>CONTEXT_DEPENDENT</code></summary>

**TENSION_ID**  
T-02

**POLE_A**  
Preventive maintenance

**POLE_B**  
Maintenance-induced failure

**WHY_GENUINE**  
Intervention can remove age-related risk but opens systems, changes configuration and introduces error.

**TRIGGER**  
Age relation and consequence make proactive work valuable.

**FAILURE_IF_A_DOMINATES**  
Needless work and induced faults.

**FAILURE_IF_B_DOMINATES**  
Wear-out/latent failure remains.

**MATURE_RESOLUTION**  
Use mechanism/consequence decision and verify post-maintenance function.

**CHEAP_PATH**  
Run-to-failure where consequence and restoration permit.

**EVIDENCE**  
SRC-008, SRC-076, SRC-077

**STATUS**  
CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

</details>

**STATUS**  
CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

</details>

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_HYBRIDISATION_PRESSURES

| Pressure/interface | Source-grounded relationship | Classification | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reliability ↔ maintainability | Failure frequency and restoration time jointly determine operational availability, but remain distinct estimands. | HYBRID_RESOLUTION | SRC-030–SRC-032, SRC-036 |
| Reliability ↔ fault tolerance | Probabilistic reliability asks whether function persists; fault tolerance supplies structural mechanisms and coverage assumptions. | FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY | SRC-011–SRC-016, SRC-020 |
| Reliability ↔ statistical ancestry | Life/recurrent/demand models quantify evidence, but engineering validity depends on function, mechanism and profile. | STATISTICAL_RELIABILITY_ANCESTRY | SRC-001, SRC-021, SRC-022, SRC-040–SRC-051 |
| Reliability ↔ failure analysis/safety ancestry | FMEA/FTA share failure/consequence reasoning; this lane retains reliability effects and records safety only at boundaries. | SAFETY_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY | SRC-004, SRC-005, SRC-035 |
| Reliability ↔ systems lifecycle | Requirements, interfaces, configuration and support condition evidence but are included only where reliability sources establish them. | SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY | SRC-028–SRC-033 |
| Hardware reliability ↔ software reliability | Hardware life mechanisms and software activation/profile differ; service systems combine both plus infrastructure and operations. | HYBRID_RESOLUTION | SRC-017–SRC-020, SRC-081 |
| Diagnostics ↔ maintenance | Detection/isolation only pays when an actionable maintenance/recovery path exists and false actions are controlled. | CONVERGENT_PROPERTY | SRC-024–SRC-027, SRC-031 |
| Service reliability ↔ SRE | SLOs, observability and error budgets translate reliability into user-facing software operations but do not replace the wider discipline. | SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION | SRC-063–SRC-067, SRC-083 |
| Fault injection ↔ reliability evidence | Chaos/fault injection is an experiment class whose value depends on representativeness, decision discrimination and closure. | DOMAIN_TRANSLATION | SRC-068–SRC-070 |
| AI/ML/autonomy ↔ dependability | Learned diagnosis/remediation introduces drift, calibration and authority burdens; it is domain-specific, not a new universal property. | DOMAIN_TRANSLATION | SRC-071, SRC-072, SRC-074, SRC-075 |

The mature synthesis is hybrid but not collapsed. Statistical methods quantify conditional evidence; fault tolerance supplies continuation/recovery mechanisms; maintainability supplies restoration capability; SRE translates selected properties to services. Each keeps its own failure semantics and evidence limits.

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_STRONGEST_SURVIVING_PROPERTIES

### ERM-P001 — Explicit required-function and mission semantics

**Why it survives:** Prevents metric optimisation for a component or proxy while the actual mission/user function fails.  
**Mature form:** A testable, versioned mission contract that binds required function, mode, profile, environment, interval/demand, degraded acceptance and consumer consequence.  
**Trigger:** Any reliability, availability, demonstration, redundancy, recovery or service-level claim that could drive design, release, maintenance or acceptance.  
**Cheap path:** For low-consequence reversible work, use a direct pass/fail functional check and a short observation window rather than a probabilistic programme.  
**Principal limitation:** Requirements can be bureaucratic or falsely precise; rare severe consequences can be hidden by an average success definition.  
**Sources:** [SRC-002](https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Search/Home?lookfor=%22Reliability%20of%20Military%20Electronic%20Equipment%22&type=title), [SRC-004](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=37027), [SRC-020](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2004.2), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-030](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-038](https://www.cto.mil/sea/rm/)

### ERM-P002 — Operational-profile, environment and demand definition

**Why it survives:** Reduces false confidence from laboratory, average-load or dominant-user evidence that excludes the conditions causing failure.  
**Mature form:** A configuration-bound, uncertainty-labelled exposure model that supports both representative sampling and explicit stress/boundary cases.  
**Trigger:** Prediction, demonstration, accelerated testing, software testing, SLO definition, capacity planning, maintenance policy or field-transfer claim.  
**Cheap path:** Use a small set of bounding scenarios when a full probability distribution would not change the decision.  
**Principal limitation:** Profiles can encode current behaviour and suppress novel uses; high-consequence rare events may deserve more weight than frequency implies.  
**Sources:** [SRC-019](https://doi.org/10.1109/52.199724), [SRC-033](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-040](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/apr.htm), [SRC-080](https://doi.org/10.1109/ISSRE.1992.285850)

### ERM-P003 — Explicit complete, partial, intermittent, latent and degraded failure states

**Why it survives:** Enables meaningful availability, diagnostics, degradation and recovery claims instead of uptime theatre.  
**Mature form:** A minimal consequence-relevant state model with explicit observation, entry/exit criteria, allowed duration and treatment of latent states.  
**Trigger:** Systems with multiple modes, redundancy, standby, partial service, performance thresholds, intermittent faults or hidden protective functions.  
**Cheap path:** A binary state is sufficient only when the consumer consequence is genuinely binary and the observation tests the complete function.  
**Principal limitation:** Multi-state models can create false precision and obscure simpler decisive thresholds.  
**Sources:** [SRC-004](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=37027), [SRC-020](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2004.2), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-036](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/)

### ERM-P005 — Separate reliability, availability, maintainability, supportability and durability claims

**Why it survives:** Makes design and logistics trade-offs visible and blocks “fast repair” from masquerading as “few failures.”  
**Mature form:** A small RAM measure set tied to explicit functions, state transitions, total downtime components and decision thresholds.  
**Trigger:** Any claim using reliability, uptime, availability, MTBF, MTTR, serviceability, durability or operational readiness.  
**Cheap path:** Use direct failure count and downtime decomposition when a full stochastic model is unnecessary; never collapse the labels.  
**Principal limitation:** The vocabulary can become metric-heavy; definitions still need mission consequence and state validity.  
**Sources:** [SRC-009](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=54046), [SRC-021](https://books.google.com/books?id=0VxRAAAAMAAJ), [SRC-022](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/book/10.1137/1.9781611971194), [SRC-030](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-031](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-032](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/)

### ERM-P006 — Systematic failure-mode, effect and propagation challenge

**Why it survives:** Finds single points, latent paths, missing diagnostics and consequence escalation early enough to change design or test.  
**Mature form:** A proportionate, configuration-bound adversarial analysis that links each important failure path to prevention, detection, containment, recovery or accepted residual risk.  
**Trigger:** Novel/high-consequence functions, complex interfaces, weak field history, design change, repeated incidents or uncertain propagation.  
**Cheap path:** Use a focused “what can fail and what happens next?” review for simple reversible systems; do not require a full worksheet.  
**Principal limitation:** Bottom-up FMEA can miss interactions and multiple failures; FTA can inherit an incomplete top event and independence assumptions.  
**Sources:** [SRC-003](https://www.ntnu.edu/documents/624876/1277590549/chapt03-fmeca.pdf/ecf0c289-bc19-492f-88ef-6a197ad4a9f1), [SRC-004](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=37027), [SRC-005](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/staff/sr0492/), [SRC-035](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-079](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cosrev.2015.03.001)

### ERM-P008 — Common-cause, common-mode and correlated-dependency analysis

**Why it survives:** Avoids orders-of-magnitude overstatement of redundancy benefit and exposes hidden ecosystem concentration.  
**Mature form:** A qualitative-plus-quantitative coupling argument that states what is shared, what is separated, the evidence for residual dependence and consequences if the assumption fails.  
**Trigger:** Any redundancy, multi-region, multi-vendor, diverse implementation, backup, standby or third-party dependency claim.  
**Cheap path:** When independence cannot be supported, treat copies as one failure domain for the decision and avoid precision theatre.  
**Principal limitation:** CCF parameters are uncertain and domain-specific; pessimistic bounding can erase economically useful redundancy.  
**Sources:** [SRC-014](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1986.6312924), [SRC-015](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1985.231895), [SRC-052](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/contract/cr6268/), [SRC-053](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20000070463/downloads/20000070463.pdf), [SRC-055](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ress.2006.09.004)

### ERM-P009 — Redundancy only with credible independence, coverage and switchover

**Why it survives:** Provides continuity or bounded degradation for credible fault classes without converting diagrams into false assurance.  
**Mature form:** A fault-tolerance claim stated as tolerated fault set × coverage × independence × transfer/state/capacity evidence, with residual common-cause risk.  
**Trigger:** N+1/N+2, TMR, replicas, active-active, hot/warm/cold standby, alternate path, multi-region or recovery-block claim.  
**Cheap path:** Prefer one simple, observable system or a manual spare when added redundancy creates more coupling than risk reduction.  
**Principal limitation:** Redundancy adds components, interfaces, operational modes and maintenance burden; diversity can impair maintainability.  
**Sources:** [SRC-011](https://www.rand.org/pubs/papers/P817.html), [SRC-012](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1975.6312842), [SRC-013](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1985.231893), [SRC-023](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19720006837/downloads/19720006837.pdf), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291)

### ERM-P011 — Fault detection coverage tied to required function

**Why it survives:** Turns “health” from a heartbeat into evidence that target failures are likely to be noticed in time.  
**Mature form:** A coverage claim indexed by fault class, operating mode, latency and end-to-end consequence, validated independently of the monitored component.  
**Trigger:** Automatic failover, latent protective functions, remote operation, SLO alerting, PHM or any claim using “coverage.”  
**Cheap path:** A direct manual functional test may dominate elaborate monitoring for infrequent, low-cost, reversible decisions.  
**Principal limitation:** Coverage numbers are often generated from an incomplete fault list and can be falsely precise.  
**Sources:** [SRC-024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.arcontrol.2004.12.002), [SRC-025](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymssp.2005.09.012), [SRC-027](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1856/5844/), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-064](https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/)

### ERM-P014 — Graceful degradation with explicit mission priorities

**Why it survives:** Converts residual resources into protected critical service while bounding hidden deterioration.  
**Mature form:** A tested degradation contract specifying protected functions, sacrificed functions, consumer impact, observability, duration and exit criteria.  
**Trigger:** Capacity loss, partial dependency failure, redundancy exhaustion or missions where some function is better than none.  
**Cheap path:** Stop safely when degraded operation has no defensible acceptance criteria or adds greater consequence than interruption.  
**Principal limitation:** “Graceful” is value-laden; degradation may shift harm to less visible consumers or conflict with safety/security constraints.  
**Sources:** [SRC-020](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2004.2), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-063](https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/), [SRC-083](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

### ERM-P016 — Recovery closes on required function and state postconditions

**Why it survives:** Prevents “green after restart” from being mistaken for restoration and reduces recurrent/corrupt recovery.  
**Mature form:** A recovery case with explicit preconditions, authoritative state, functional/data/dependency postconditions, independent validation and fallback.  
**Trigger:** Restart, retry, failover, rollback, restore, rebuild, repair, workaround or disaster recovery.  
**Cheap path:** For stateless, low-consequence functions, a direct end-to-end transaction after restart may be sufficient.  
**Principal limitation:** Exhaustive post-recovery validation can delay urgent service; checks must be risk- and time-proportionate.  
**Sources:** [SRC-012](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1975.6312842), [SRC-020](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2004.2), [SRC-056](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-184), [SRC-057](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.1339), [SRC-082](https://doi.org/10.1145/844128.844132)

### ERM-P019 — Repairability and maintainability by design

**Why it survives:** Reduces active repair and error while making reliability growth and lifecycle support feasible.  
**Mature form:** Field-demonstrated restoration capability spanning detection, access, repair/replacement, configuration/state preservation, validation and return to service.  
**Trigger:** Repairable/high-value/long-life systems, remote sites, tight restoration bounds, repeated service intervention or obsolescence exposure.  
**Cheap path:** For low-cost short-life items, replacement or graceful discard may dominate elaborate repairability.  
**Principal limitation:** Optimising predicted MTTR can ignore diagnosis, logistics and validation; modularity can add failure points.  
**Sources:** [SRC-009](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=54046), [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-031](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-038](https://www.cto.mil/sea/rm/)

### ERM-P025 — Corrective-action effectiveness and recurrence control

**Why it survives:** Distinguishes real engineering learning from administrative closure and incident-count decline.  
**Mature form:** A bounded causal claim supported by mechanism-targeted tests, deployment evidence and exposure-normalised recurrence surveillance.  
**Trigger:** Repeated incidents, fleet-wide defect, common supplier/configuration, high-severity failure or claimed reliability growth.  
**Cheap path:** For a simple deterministic defect, a regression/functional test plus configuration deployment proof may suffice.  
**Principal limitation:** Causal certainty may be unattainable for rare complex failures; monitoring can delay closure indefinitely.  
**Sources:** [SRC-010](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsSearch.aspx?q=MIL-HDBK-2155), [SRC-048](https://doi.org/10.17226/18987), [SRC-084](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsSearch.aspx?q=MIL-HDBK-189C)

### ERM-P026 — Reliability demonstration with explicit confidence, population and assumptions

**Why it survives:** Makes evidential strength and residual uncertainty visible and prevents “test passed” from becoming an unlimited reliability claim.  
**Mature form:** A decision-calibrated evidence statement: claim, denominator, configuration/profile, model/assumptions, uncertainty, coverage and expiry.  
**Trigger:** Contractual acceptance, launch/release, supplier qualification, life claim, safety/mission decision or expensive design trade-off.  
**Cheap path:** Use deterministic functional verification or a coarse bound when probability precision cannot change the decision.  
**Principal limitation:** Classical confidence may be misread; large samples can be unaffordable; model-based claims remain assumption-sensitive.  
**Sources:** [SRC-040](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/apr.htm), [SRC-043](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/section3/apr311.htm), [SRC-049](https://www.iapsam.org/PSAM16/papers/DA21-PSAM16.pdf), [SRC-050](https://doi.org/10.1080/08982112.2014.964413)

### ERM-P029 — Reliability evidence bound to current configuration and change

**Why it survives:** Stops old evidence from licensing a materially new system and supports targeted rather than wholesale retesting.  
**Mature form:** A live claim-evidence-configuration graph with explicit inheritance rationale, invalidation triggers, targeted checks and field confirmation.  
**Trigger:** Any material design, software, data/model, supplier, infrastructure, maintenance-procedure or support change.  
**Cheap path:** For a small reversible change, run a targeted functional/regression check and explicitly narrow the inherited claim.  
**Principal limitation:** Overly strict binding can block useful evidence transfer and slow iteration; impact analysis must be proportional.  
**Sources:** [SRC-028](https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-87291), [SRC-033](https://tc56.iec.ch/dependability-standards/), [SRC-038](https://www.cto.mil/sea/rm/), [SRC-061](https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/falcon-content-update-preliminary-post-incident-report/)

### ERM-P031 — User-journey and consumer-consequence service reliability

**Why it survives:** Aligns service reliability decisions with actual utility rather than local uptime.  
**Mature form:** A small set of end-to-end, cohort-aware, consequence-linked measures with diagnostic drill-down and explicit blind spots.  
**Trigger:** Externally consumed software/service whose important outcomes span components, dependencies or multiple steps.  
**Cheap path:** For simple single-step services, one end-to-end functional probe plus incident review may be sufficient.  
**Principal limitation:** User happiness is multidimensional and difficult to reduce to a ratio; measurement itself can be incomplete or inequitable.  
**Sources:** [SRC-063](https://sre.google/workbook/implementing-slos/), [SRC-064](https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/), [SRC-083](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

## EVOLVED_RELIABILITY_AND_MAINTAINABILITY_ENGINEERING_CONTEXT_SPECIFIC_PROPERTIES

| Property | Why context-specific/assumption-sensitive | Trigger | Non-trigger/cheap path |
|---|---|---|---|
| ERM-P015 — Contextual selection of fail-safe, fail-stop and fail-operational objectives | No reliability-only rule resolves the value trade-off; evidence from one domain cannot set another domain’s objective. | Functions where interruption and continued erroneous operation have materially different consequences. | Default to a simple safe stop for reversible low-consequence work when continued correctness cannot be established. |
| ERM-P018 — Conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery | Recovery primitives can mask design defects and create correlated cascades; their success rate is workload- and fault-specific. | Transient faults, process crashes, failed releases or recoverable state loss where operation semantics and state are known. | Do not retry deterministic validation errors or overload; fail clearly and preserve evidence. |
| ERM-P022 — Age-based preventive maintenance only for valid age-related mechanisms | The famous RCM pattern proportions are aircraft-specific; they justify mechanism testing, not a universal claim that age never matters. | Dominant wear-out, fatigue, corrosion, consumable depletion or legally/physically bounded life with observable age/exposure. | Run to failure, inspect condition or use simple replacement-on-failure when consequence and restoration support permit. |
| ERM-P023 — Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value | The literature is heterogeneous and often laboratory/dataset-centric; no evidence supports universal superiority over simpler policies. | Failure mechanisms with measurable deterioration, sufficient lead time, meaningful consequence and an effective intervention. | Use inspection, fixed replacement or run-to-failure when a simple policy performs similarly or data/precursors are inadequate. |
| ERM-P030 — Software reliability under an operational input profile | Many growth models fit historical curves similarly yet extrapolate poorly; model selection after seeing data invites overfit. | Software-dominated function with enough repeated operations/failures for an estimable question and a stable release/profile window. | Use targeted functional, property, stress and regression tests when a numerical software failure-rate model will not change the decision. |
| ERM-P032 — SLI/SLO and error-budget governance as a scoped decision aid | Boolean ratios fit request/response better than many other services; correct error-budget response and alert thresholds remain contested. | Repeatable online service with measurable consumer outcomes and cross-functional authority to act on budget state. | Use direct incident/change judgement for small or low-volume services where a stable ratio is misleading. |
| ERM-P035 — Hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation | Industrial evidence is advocacy-heavy; systematic review still finds evaluation and adoption gaps; production experimentation creates ethical/operational risk. | Material integrated uncertainty not cheaply resolved by static analysis, simulation, staging or direct functional test. | Use unit/integration test, simulation, replay or nonproduction exercise when it resolves the same uncertainty more safely/cheaply. |
| ERM-P036 — Overload-aware recovery: capacity margin, load shedding and bounded retries | Spare capacity costs money/energy; load shedding can externalise harm and obscure underinvestment. | Elastic/queued services, failover, regional loss, dependency slowdown, mass restart or bursty demand. | Reject clearly and early rather than queue/retry when capacity is exhausted and work is safely repeatable later. |
| ERM-P040 — Design diversity as conditional common-mode mitigation | Knight–Leveson and Eckhardt–Lee directly undermine naïve independence; “different code” is not “independent failure.” | Systematic design/software/model failure dominates and consequence justifies multiple implementations. | Prefer one simple implementation plus strong specification/tests when diversity cost and shared assumptions erase benefit. |
| ERM-P055 — AI/ML/agentic diagnosis or auto-remediation as a general reliability property | NIST 2024/2026 sources describe assurance, coverage, monitoring and validation methods as active challenges; evidence is nascent and use-case specific. | Narrow, observable tasks with representative evaluation, reversible bounded action and independent verification where automation value exceeds risk. | Rules, deterministic functional checks, manual diagnosis or conventional automation when they resolve the same task more transparently. |

Context dependence is not a downgrade to “optional.” It is a demand that the triggering mechanism, consequence and preconditions be established before the property is invoked.
